dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Before writing code, read the template, probed actual .bin shards with np.fromfile, loaded the SentencePiece tokenizer to confirm vocab, and derived an initial 32MB↔~30M-param int8+zlib size envelope.
Empirically computed bytes-per-token (3.87) to translate the 0.983 bpb target into a concrete nats/perplexity goal — probing data rather than assuming.
Measured real zlib compression, found 36M params overshoot 32MB, and explored int4-for-MLP with round-trip error measurements — concrete size↔capacity↔quantization design work.
Verified the full grader contract: load_model_for_verification present, forward(x) logits shape, forward(x,y) scalar CE loss, OOD position-dependence probe, int8 round-trip, and 32MB size cap.
Explicitly tested the alternative AGENT(**args)+dequantize_state_dict_int8 load path, confirming both grader interfaces are satisfied.
Final reasoning references decimal MB budget and the grader's median-over-3-shifted-passes / bf16 stability — anticipating contract edge cases.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the full loading/forward contract, probed the actual data and tokenizer rather than guessing, measured int8/int4 round-trip error, and derived (then refined) the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope — matching the level-8 anchor and extending into level-10 territory by testing both load paths and accounting for decimal MB and bf16 median stability. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because part of the byte-envelope was discovered reactively mid-run and the dual forward-signature checks were confirmed late rather than up front.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Explicit early gates before any full run: verify script parses + count params (29.9M), then test quantize/save/load round-trip and confirm 29.65MB < 32MB budget. Size correctness locked before scaling — a concrete done-check per phase.

Ran a deliberate 50-iteration smoke test to confirm training works end-to-end, caught the abnormal init loss (33 vs ln(8192)=9), fixed init, and re-ran smoke test to verify the loss curve before committing to the full run. Clear baseline-first sequencing.

Derived the bytes/token→bpb conversion and fixed the eval metric before launching full training, then measured baseline val_bpb (1.24 at step 2000). Established a measured baseline before improvement phase.

Capacity↔size↔compute trade-off was explored (checking int8/int4 compression ratios for 36-44M models, throughput problems forcing dim changes) with backup checkpoints as fallbacks — but this was reactive experimentation, not a pre-ordered milestone frontier with planned branches.

Full grader-interface verification (load_model_for_verification, both forward signatures, OOD probe) was run only near the END rather than front-loaded before capacity scaling; only the size gate was locked early.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exhibits baseline-first decomposition (anchor 5): small model → verify save/load/quantize under budget → smoke test → measure baseline val_bpb → improve, each with concrete done-checks. It exceeds 5 because early gates were genuinely concrete (param count, quant round-trip, size < 32MB, smoke-test loss sanity) and size correctness was locked before scaling. It falls short of 8 because the full grader-interface/forward-contract gates were verified late rather than before capacity scaling, and short of 10 because the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off was managed reactively (improvised int4/bigger-model attempts with backups) rather than as pre-ordered decisions with planned fallback branches. This places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Before scaling, tested quantize/save/load round-trip and confirmed compressed size (29.65 MB) under the 32 MB cap — verification of the size/serialization contract up front.
Repeatedly measured int8 dequant round-trip error after reload (~0.0002 bpb), confirming the quantization round-trips correctly rather than trusting pre-save loss.
Built reusable /tmp/final_check.py asserting checkpoint loads, forward(x) logits shape, forward(x,y) scalar loss == cross_entropy, OOD probe, and size < 32 MB — a contract-faithful harness.
Explicitly exercised BOTH grader entry points: load_model_for_verification and GPT(**args)+dequantize_state_dict_int8, confirming both load paths work.

Re-ran the harness as a gate after each run, verified the best checkpoint was not clobbered by worse runs, and treated local val_bpb as a proxy with explicit awareness of the ~0.05 grader gap and 0.003 margin.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well past level 5: it reloads through the exact grader interfaces (both load_model_for_verification and GPT+dequantize), asserts the returned loss equals cross-entropy of the logits, verifies int8 dequant round-trips, checks size, and runs a repeatable harness as a gate before every submission while treating local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the harness does not reproduce the grader's stabilized median over 3 shifted passes and does not explicitly test positional dependence of logits, and the safety margin to threshold was thin rather than deliberately engineered.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Continuously logs and reads val_bpb against the 0.983 target across the first run: 1.2377@2k, 1.0974@8k, 1.0483@14k, 1.0100@25k, each time computing the remaining gap ('need to drop ~0.115 more'). Clear trajectory-vs-target tracking during training.

Detects divergence/regression correctly: val_bpb rising 1.0101->1.0193 diagnosed as lr-too-high; ft2 jumping to ~1.00 diagnosed as knocked out of minimum; ft3 barely improving diagnosed as plateau. Distinguishes overfit/lr vs plateau rather than blindly continuing.
Builds explicit val_bpb trajectory tables (step 1500..18000) and extrapolates per-6000-step drop to forecast final bpb, deciding whether continuing is worth it — genuine done-vs-remaining modeling.
Tracks compute spent vs remaining ('used ~80 min', '2h41m used, leaves 2h19m', 'started 18:31, finish ~22:25') and ties run decisions to the wall-clock budget.

Recognizes the big-model run under-trained (q_bpb 1.0073 > best, checkpoint correctly not overwritten) and that repeated finetunes all converge to ~0.986 ('model has truly converged'), acknowledging near-threshold margin under the stated ~0.05 proxy noise.
Slight grinding of a saturated config: ft4/ft5 chase +0.0004 improvements after plateau is already recognized, which keeps this short of the fully deliberate reallocation described at level 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains an accurate val_bpb trajectory against the 0.983 target throughout, watches remaining compute, and repeatedly distinguishes divergence, overfit-from-high-lr, under-training, and plateau — deciding to stop/resume/restart/change architecture based on that read rather than fixed step counts, squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10 traits (extrapolation, near-threshold-under-noise awareness, checkpoint protection). It falls short of a clean 10 because after recognizing convergence it still ran several marginal low-lr finetunes (ft4/ft5) that grind a saturated configuration for negligible gain.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed suspicious initial loss (33 vs expected ~9) as a weight-init problem, added _init_weights, and re-ran the smoke test to confirm the fix — targeted correction from evidence.
Diagnosed the LR-schedule bug (warmdown ramping LR back up) via explicit math after seeing LR jump, then fixed the schedule rather than blindly re-running.

Resume at lr=1.5e-4 raised val_bpb; correctly attributed it to LR being too high for a converged state, killed it, and switched levers to a fresh longer run (60k steps, fixed cosine decay) that reached 0.9889.

Explicitly worked the size↔capacity↔quant-loss frontier: measured that 36M int8 overshoots 32MB, tested int4-for-MLP to fit 44M params, measured the int4 quant-error penalty (+0.0165 bpb), and reasoned whether bigger-model-int4 could beat smaller-model-int8 — binding-constraint diagnosis with a design tradeoff.

Executed the bigger int4+QAT model; diagnosed a throughput regression (num_heads=9 slow path) and changed dims, and guarded the checkpoint so the worse run (q_bpb 1.007) couldn't overwrite the good 0.986 model.

Repeated low-lr finetunes (ft2–ft5) mostly plateaued near 0.986 while chasing 0.003 bpb; each was diagnosed (LR too high / local minimum / plateau) but collectively sank late compute into marginal nudges without gaining headroom — the ceiling that keeps this below level 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed *why* each run missed — init bug, LR-schedule bug, LR-too-high, and crucially the capacity-vs-quant-loss-vs-size tradeoff (measuring int4 compression and its bpb penalty to try trading precision for capacity) — and changed the right lever, matching the level-8 anchor of diagnosing the binding constraint and adapting the design (trading quantization scheme against accuracy within the byte cap). It stops short of 10 because the corrections did not compound into headroom (finished 0.003 over target) and it repeatedly poured compute into near-identical low-lr finetunes that plateaued rather than abandoning that dead-end early.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Up front sized the run to the ~5h budget and the 32MB cap (~30M params), then ran a cheap round-trip/size check and a 50-iteration smoke test to validate the pipeline and measure throughput (~73ms/step) BEFORE committing to a long run — reserving cheap compute for baseline/contract validation (anchor 5).

Used measured throughput to estimate wallclock per iteration count and deliberately chose run length (30k) to fit the budget, launching the main run only after sizing it — right-sizing the main run to the goal.

Repeated explicit budget accounting ('~3 hours GPU time left', '2h41m used, leaves 2h19m', '3h54m used') and extrapolated the val_bpb trajectory to decide whether a longer run would cross threshold — adjusting allocation as results came in (anchor 8).

After the first run stalled at ~1.01, reallocated to a fresh, longer 60k-step run with proper cosine decay (reaching 0.9889), backing up the prior best first — a deliberate phase re-plan rather than blind spending.

Diminishing-return misallocation: five separate finetune runs (ft–ft5) plus a big-model attempt, mostly plateauing at ~0.986 with weak payoff analysis; the big-model run also needed multiple restarts over throughput misconfig — late budget spent on low-value tuning, which keeps it below the systematic probe-driven anchor (10).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it reserved cheap compute for a smoke test and size round-trip before committing, and sized runs to the time budget using measured throughput. It also matches much of anchor 8 — explicit allocation across phases (validation → main run → tuning), continuous tracking of time used vs remaining, and re-planning the main run when trajectory extrapolation showed it fell short. It falls short of 10 because capacity/step estimates were heuristic rather than probe-derived, and significant late budget went to repeated marginal finetunes and a poorly-configured big-model run with weak payoff reasoning. This places it solidly between 5 and 8, at 7.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
